articles.title: Man City Premier League charges explained: What are they? What could punishment be? What happens next?
articles.summary: Man City were charged by the Premier League with more than 100 alleged breaches of the league's financial rules back in February 2023; the hearing led by independent commission concluded in December 2024; Inquiry moves to appeal stage amid reports majority of charges 'proven'
articles.body:
There are reports that an independent tribunal has reached decisions in Manchester City's 115 charges case.

The reports claim that most of the charges were found to have been proven. Sky Sports News understands that the process is moving to the appeal stage .

The Premier League is not commenting as this is a private and confidential process. It will not be providing any guidance.

A Manchester City spokesperson said: "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC's position remains consistent with the club's statement of February 2023.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

Manchester City have been charged with breaking Financial Fair Play rules over a nine-year period, which started in 2009 and went on until 2018. They have also been charged with failing to co-operate with Premier League investigations into their finances.

When the Premier League charged City in 2023, its press release detailed alleged rules breaches that added up to 115 in number, but it is believed that the actual number is 130.

During the period in question, Man City, who have denied all the charges against them, won the Premier League three times.

The Premier League's Financial Fair Play (FFP) rules are designed to ensure clubs pretty much spend what they earn. You can get around those potentially by inflating how much you're earning or hiding how much you are spending. In the PSR (Profitability and Sustainability Rules) and FFP era, artificially increasing your revenue could, in theory, allow a club to spend more on transfers and wages.

According to the Premier League, Man City broke the rules over nine seasons by allegedly failing to provide accurate financial information.

Among the charges against City are that they didn't fully disclose the financial remunerations that were made to one of their managers over a four-year period. The suggestion is that there was a secret contract so one of the managers was getting paid much more than officially stated.

The Premier League also alleges Man City did not comply with UEFA's FFP rules over a five-year period.

The alleged rule breaches first came to light in a series of articles published by Der Spiegel in Germany in 2018. They were based on emails obtained by convicted Portuguese hacker Rui Pinto, which also appeared on the Football Leaks website.

It was this story that started a UEFA investigation into Man City in 2019, as well as a Premier League investigation.

In February 2020 City were found guilty of breaking UEFA's FFP rules and given a two-year European ban and €30m fine - but the ban was lifted by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) five months later and the fine reduced to €10m.

CAS said City showed "blatant disregard of UEFA's investigative process" but cleared them of "disguising equity funds as sponsorship contribution". The ruling stated that most of the alleged breaches "were either not established or time-barred," with UEFA statute only allowing prosecutions within a five-year period.

City said that the CAS ruling was "validation of the club's position and the body of evidence that it was able to present".

But the Premier League does not have a cut-off for investigating alleged breaches, which is why it has brought charges against the club going back to 2009.

When the Premier League eventually brought charges against City in February 2023, the club said they were "surprised" by the development and insisted their position was supported by a "comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence".

City's hearing in the case against the Premier League ran from September 16 to December 6 2024.

The 12-week hearing was held in front of a three-person independent commission at the International Dispute Resolution Centre in London.

The timeframe between the hearing and the judgment was always expected to take several months because of the volume of charges and the amount of information to be reviewed.

If the commission rules against City, it can punish them in any way it sees fit.

According to Premier League rules, the sanction could be a points deduction, a fine or even expulsion from the Premier League.

Anything is possible because the Premier League does not have set sanctions for financial rule breaches. Clubs decided not to have them because there were fears clubs would break the rules and take the punishment if they knew what that punishment was going to be.

In February 2025, Richard Masters said the Premier League was looking at having a 'sanctions grid' - setting out agreed sanctions for different rules breaches - but that is not yet in place.

Everton were deducted six and then two points during the 2023/24 season for PSR breaches, while Nottingham Forest were deducted four points that same season.

Further back, Luton Town - when in the EFL - were deducted 30 points in 2008/09 - 10 for illegal payments to agents and 20 for exiting administration without the required insolvency procedure of a Company Voluntary Arrangement.

More recently in 2021/22, Derby County, also in the EFL, were deducted 21 points - 12 for administration and nine for financial irregularities.

If any of the breaches are proven, it is highly likely City will appeal. In 2014 City chairman Khaldoon al-Mubarak said he would rather spend £30m on the best 50 lawyers in the world and sue UEFA for the next 10 years than agree a financial penalty for alleged FFP breaches.

In this case both sides can appeal within 14 days of the judgment. Any appeal would be heard by a new three-person commission. A judgement can be appealed on grounds such as fraud, misconduct, or gross unfairness by the arbitrator. City cannot appeal to CAS.

A party to the proceedings which wishes to challenge a decision of the Commission may do so under Section W of the Premier League Rules.

The Appeal Board is also appointed by the chair of the independent judicial panel Sir Gary Hickinbottom and must have three members, one of whom should have held judicial office, and would sit as the chair of the Appeal Board.

The proceedings of the Appeal Board are also confidential and heard in private.

The Appeal Board has wide discretion in respect of the appeal, and may allow it, dismiss it, or make any order that it deems fit (including varying the order of Commission).

articles.title: Man City Premier League charges: Inquiry moves to appeal stage amid reports majority of charges 'proven'
articles.summary: An independent tribunal has reached decisions in Manchester City's 115 charges case, according to reports.
articles.body:
The reports claim that most of the charges were found to have been proven.

Sky Sports News understands that the process is moving to the appeal stage.

The Premier League is not commenting as this is a private and confidential process. It will not be providing any guidance.

A Manchester City spokesperson said: "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC's position remains consistent with the club's statement of February 2023.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

"City were charged with breaking the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018 and also failing to cooperate with the Premier League investigation between 2019 and 2023. It is very important to stress that City deny any wrongdoing and they've always said that their defence is supported by a body of irrefutable evidence.

"Fifty-four charges are to do with failing to provide accurate financial information. Thirty-five charges to do with failing to co-operate with the Premier League investigations between December 2018 and February 2023.

"Fourteen charges relate to a failure to provide accurate details for player and manager payments from 2009-10 season and also the 2017-18 season. And seven charges were to do with breaching the Premier League's profitability and sustainability rules in two seasons 2015-16 and 2017-18, and also five charges relating to failing to comply with UEFA's rules, including Financial Fair Play rules in the 2013-14 and 2017-18 seasons."

"If the commission rules against City, it can punish them in any way it sees fit.

"According to Premier League rules, the sanction could be a points deduction, a fine or even expulsion from the Premier League.

"Anything is possible because the Premier League does not have set sanctions for financial rule breaches. Clubs decided not to have them because there were fears clubs would break the rules and take the punishment if they knew what that punishment was going to be.

"In February 2025 Richard Masters said the Premier League was looking at having a 'sanctions grid' - setting out agreed sanctions for different rules breaches - but that is not yet in place.

"Everton were deducted six and then two points during the 2023/24 season for PSR breaches, while Nottingham Forest were deducted four points that same season.

"Luton Town were deducted 30 points in 2008/09 (10 for illegal payments to agents and 20 for exiting administration without a CVA).

"In 2021/22 Derby County were deducted 21 points (12 for administration and nine for financial irregularities)."

articles.title: What punishment could Man City face after Premier League charges verdict and will they appeal?
articles.summary: It has taken more than two years, but a judgement finally appears to have been made on the 115 charges levelled against Man City. Here's what it means.
articles.body:
It has taken more than two years, but a judgement finally appears to have been reached on the 115 charges levelled against Manchester City over breaches of Premier League financial rules.

Following a four-year investigation, City were charged and the hearing finally got under way on 16 September 2024.

BBC Sport has now learned a decision has been made, after the Athletic reported City had been found guilty on all almost of the charges.

We are not at the end of this process, however. Far from it.

But what does this mean for City's titles? What about their Premier League status? Will there be an appeal? And how long will it be before this saga does come to an end?

Man City found guilty of majority of 115 financial rule breaches - sources tell BBC

In February 2023, City were charged and referred to an independent commission over alleged breaches that were said to have taken place between 2009 and 2018.

The charges - relating to Premier League financial rules - are:

54 x failure to provide accurate financial information from 2009-10 to 2017-18.

14 x failure to provide accurate details for player and manager payments from 2009-10 to 2017-18.

5 x failure to comply with Uefa's rules including financial fair play (FFP) 2013-14 to 2017-18.

7 x breaching Premier League profit and sustainability (PSR) rules from 2015-16 to 2017-18.

35 x failure to co-operate with Premier League investigations from December 2018 to Feb 2023.

City have always denied wrongdoing and BBC Sport has been told they would appeal were they found guilty.

German newspaper Der Spiegel published leaked documents, including emails purportedly sent between top City executives (some of whom remain at the City Football Group), across several seasons following the club's Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008.

It alleged these showed the club had inflated sponsorship revenue from state-owned airline Etihad and state-controlled telecoms firm Etisalat by disguising direct investment from their holding company (Sheik Mansour's Abu Dhabi United Group, or ADUG) as sponsorship income by channelling the funds through the companies' accounts.

This, it was alleged, was a means of meeting FFP rules introduced by Uefa in 2011 - and PSR brought in by the Premier League in 2012 - limiting clubs' permitted losses.

There then followed further allegations of misreporting financial information centred on documents that claimed to show secret 'off-the-books' payments to then manager Roberto Mancini via consultancy fees from a club in Abu Dhabi.

It is also alleged the club gave players more money than was officially going through the accounts so recorded spending was less than it actually was.

City, who have always maintained ADUG is a private fund rather than an arm of the state, refused to comment on any of Der Spiegel's revelations, saying the leaked emails were obtained illegally, and they were an "attempt to damage the club's reputation".

City - along with the companies involved - strongly denied breaking any financial rules. But that did not stop both Uefa and the Premier League launching investigations as a result.

November 2018: Football Leaks allegations emerge with Der Spiegel publishing claims Manchester City breached financial fair play rules.

March 2019: Uefa launches a formal investigation off the back of Der Spiegel's findings.

May 2019: City criticise the investigation and launch an appeal process.

November 2019: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) deems City's appeal inadmissible.

February 2020: Uefa announces a two-year ban for City from European competitions and a €30m fine.

July 2020: City's European ban is overturned after an appeal to Cas.

July 2021: City lose a jurisdiction ruling that allows the media to report the Premier League is continuing to investigate the champions for alleged financial breaches.

April 2022: Der Spiegel publishes a fresh report claiming the Premier League has been investigating the club for three years, providing detailed claims.

February 2023: The Premier League charges City with 115 financial breaches.

September 2024: The start of a 10-week hearing between the Premier League and City on the 115 charges.

February 2025: City manager Pep Guardiola says the club expect to learn the verdict "within one month". Guardiola left the Etihad at the end of last season.

September 2026: Reports emerge that a verdict has been reached, with sources telling the BBC that City have been found guilty of breaking the majority of the charges.

It was never expected the verdict would come complete with the sanctions.

We now face a waiting game for even that verdict to officially be made public by the independent panel.

We don't know who was on the panel that heard and ruled on the case, and that will only come once a written judgment is released.

All options are open to the disciplinary commission:

Points deduction (immediate or suspended).

Financial penalties (immediate or suspended).

Being removed from the Premier League would mean City lose their membership and are demoted to a lower division from the end of the season.

That could also happen through a points penalty so severe they would effectively be relegated.

The Premier League declined to comment on the case when approached on Friday.

City issued a statement that showed frustration news of the verdict had leaked.

It read: "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality.

"As such Manchester City FC's position remains consistent with the club's statement of February 2023.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

Will there be an appeal? How long would one take?

An appeal from City is expected to be a formality.

City's legal team is being led by Lord Pannick KC, who is reported to charge £5,000 an hour for his services. He helped City overturn their two-year European ban in 2020.

However, considering we are already eight years into this process - and two years beyond the start of the hearing itself - it is impossible to speculate when this could come to an end.

Until now, the case has been watertight, with no media leaks from any of the parties involved.

However, while the commission's judgement can be directly appealed against, it is not possible for City to take it to Cas.

What titles did City win and who was affected?

City won the Premier League three times during the period in question.

That includes their first in the Premier League era in 2011-12, plus 2013-14 and 2017-18.

They won the FA Cup in 2011, and the EFL Cup three times - 2013-14, 2015-16 and 2017-18.

Since their 2008 takeover by ADUG, City have won eight league titles, and multiple cups including the Champions League as part of a Treble in 2023.

If the commission choses to hand City's titles to other clubs, this is who could benefit:

Could affected clubs claim compensation from City?

Earlier this year, Everton were told they must pay Burnley £35m over the impact of a breach of the Premier League's financial rules.

The case - heard by a Premier League commission - relates to the 2021-22 season, when Everton were found to have broken PSR regulations over a three-year period.

Burnley argued the breach impacted their chances of staying in the Premier League, and sought compensation for the losses associated with being relegated.

The Clarets were awarded £26m in damages and a further £9m in interest.

Clubs who had their league positions impacted by City's offences could potentially claim a loss of chance to win potential honours.

These would need to be individually heard by an independent commission.

Everton told to pay Burnley £35m over PSR breach

This specific case was six years in the making, so legal fees on both sides were estimated at tens of millions of pounds before the hearing even started.

Whichever side 'wins' can be expected to make a claim for costs.

For context, the Premier League wanted Everton to pay the full £4.9m legal costs of their first PSR six-point deduction case.

However, an appeal board ruled Everton should pay £1.7m and the Premier League cover the remaining £3.2m legal fees.

Any costs being paid by the Premier League at the end of the City case would have to be spread across the 20 clubs which make up the league.

Have there been other cases involving Premier League teams?

Comparisons have been drawn to the cases brought by the Premier League against Nottingham Forest and Everton respectively over breaches of PSR.

During the 2023-24 season, both clubs were docked points for making more losses than they were permitted to for the three-year period from the 2020-21 to 2022-23 seasons.

Those cases were of a single charge, were easier to decipher and involved significantly less evidence.

Everton were twice deducted points. For the first charge, they were docked six points - reduced from 10 points on appeal. The second offence led to them being handed a two-point penalty.

Everton docked two points for second financial breach

Forest docked four points for financial rules breach

Why are the Man City and Chelsea cases different?

Chelsea faced 74 charges of rule breaches, but these were quite different and primarily focused on transfers that happened between the 2010-11 and 2015-16 seasons, including deals for Eden Hazard, Samuel Eto'o and Willian.

The Premier League fined Chelsea £10m and handed out a suspended transfer ban after they admitted making £47m in secret payments.

Importantly, Chelsea reached a settlement with the Premier League in relation to historical regulatory matters that were self-reported.

This has not been the case with City, who have always denied wrongdoing.

The Blues were also fined by Uefa and the Football Association.

Chelsea fined but avoid suspended points deduction

Pre-match, post-match and topical City content

articles.title: Celtic and Rangers appeal Scottish FA behind closed doors sanction after Old Firm crowd trouble
articles.summary: The Old Firm clubs were ordered to play their next Scottish Cup home ties behind closed doors following crowd trouble at their quarter-final fixture in March; Celtic and Rangers fans clashed on the pitch at Ibrox and 43 people were arrested; an appeal hearing will take place on October 26
articles.body:
The Old Firm sides have also challenged the £100,000 sum they were ordered to pay the opposition club for that match.

The punishment ruled a second match would be behind closed doors if there is any trouble at a Scottish Cup fixture until the end of next season.

It followed their quarter-final meeting last season that ended with fans from both sides clashing on the pitch at Ibrox .

Police Scotland arrested 43 people following the scenes that left officers injured as missiles and pyros were launched.

An appeal hearing will take place on October 26.

This was the first Old Firm game at Ibrox since 2018 where Celtic were given the full Broomloan Stand, meaning there were around 7,500 away fans at the game, while some broke into the away end before kick-off too. That figure was in place to comply with Scottish Cup rules on ticket allocations.

The league match between Rangers and Celtic the previous weekend had around 2,500 away fans after an agreement between clubs to give around five per cent of stadium capacity to away teams for this fixture.

That followed seasons of reduced allocations, or at times no away fans at games.

Celtic progressed to the semi-finals with a 4-2 shoot-out victory over Rangers after the goalless draw at Ibrox, which sparked a pitch invasion from both sets of supporters.

Some visiting fans spilled onto the playing surface to celebrate after the winning spot-kick and supporters from the Rangers end charged towards them with fireworks thrown back and forth.

A total of 43 arrests have now been made after the scenes at Ibrox.

Following the punishment, Celtic said they were "shocked" by the "disproportionate punishment".

Rangers then allocated just 300 tickets to Celtic for their League Cup match at Ibrox this month .

The Ibrox side said that decision had been made based on the independent report that was commissioned following the Scottish Cup quarter-final in March.

They added that since that fixture in March "there have also been further pitch invasions involving Celtic supporters".

Celtic rejected the proposal, and it resulted in the SPFL intervening, with the determination being that no away fans would be permitted at Old Firm matches this season in the Scottish Premiership and League Cup.

An independent review into the scenes previously concluded that "crushing" and "life-threatening violence" were narrowly avoided.

The report, led by Mark Blackbourne, found: "The Celtic Ultras were the first to enter the pitch in jubilation, with others following their lead.

"In contrast, the Union Bears' movement onto the track and towards the pitch was reactionary, confrontational, and overtly threatening. In both cases, the proximity of these groups to the playing surface materially increased the likelihood of a mass incursion and contributed to the rapid escalation of disorder.

"The post-match pitch invasion by several hundred Celtic supporters was wholly inexcusable. It provoked an immediate hostile response from sections of the home support, who forced past stewards and police to reach the pitch."

Mr Blackbourne also noted it is "deeply disturbing" that a post-match Glasgow City Council Special SAG meeting recorded that time-served Police Scotland officers were described as "petrified" of policing another match at Ibrox Stadium.

He added: "That word must be read in context, not in isolation, but so qualified, it remains deeply disturbing for Scottish football.

"This reference demands the most serious attention from all parties with responsibility for the governance of safety and security at major football fixtures in Scotland."

Interviewees independently described the organisational characteristics of certain Ultra groups in terms more commonly associated with organised crime groups in the report.

The report called for incidents linked to Ultra groups to come down with heavier sanctions from the clubs.

articles.title: Curt Cignetti Tells Indiana Fans Not to 'B---h' About Shutout Win vs. Western Kentucky
articles.summary: The burden of expectations has resulted in a handful of Indiana football fans expressing some concern about last week's 38-0 win over Western Kentucky because it wasn't a larger margin of victory.
articles.body:
The burden of expectations has resulted in a handful of Indiana football fans expressing some concern about last week's 38-0 win over Western Kentucky because it wasn't a larger margin of victory.

Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti's response to the fan reaction was telling them not to "b---h" about a 38-point win.

"What are we, 29-2? When I came, I saw the pictures, 10,000 people in the stands. Don't b---h about a 38-0 win," Cignetti said during an appearance on the Kirkwood and Dunn podcast.

Expert CFB Locks for Week 4's Biggest Games 🔒

Ranking the Most NFL Pro-Ready College Football Athletes 🔢

Cignetti actually undersold his record at Indiana because last week's win improved it to 30-2, including 19 straight wins since the start of the 2025 season.

The Hoosiers entered their matchup with Western Kentucky favored by 44.5 points, per FanDuel Sportsbook . It was the third time in three games this season they have failed to cover the spread, though their average margin of victory so far is still 43.0 points per contest.

It is strange how fast the tide has turned for Indiana since Cignetti arrived. Before the 2024 season, a 38-0 win over any program would have been a cause for celebration in Bloomington.

Now, there is a huge microscope closely watching Indiana games. It doesn't help Cignetti's case that the Hoosiers' non-conference schedule was lacking in high-end competition.

Per ESPN's FPI metric, Indiana has played the fourth-easiest schedule out of 138 FBS programs thus far. The Big Ten has three of the four teams at the bottom of that list, including Indiana, Washington and Nebraska.

Cignetti will get the chance to show fans how good this year's Hoosiers team is as they get ready to start conference play. They will host undefeated Northwestern on Friday night.

The real gauntlet for Indiana begins on Oct. 17 when it kicks off a run that includes matchups with Ohio State, Michigan and USC in the span of five weeks.

articles.title: El nuevo 'Joselu' de La Fábrica se gana su primer ascenso
articles.standfirst: Fran Santamaría, el sorprendente '9' llegado este verano al Juvenil A, se entrena con el Real Madrid C y apunta a su primera convocatoria como refuerzo de lujo para el derbi del domingo
articles.summary: Fran Santamaría, el sorprendente '9' llegado este verano al Juvenil A, se entrena con el Madrid C y apunta a su primera convocatoria para el derbi del domingo
articles.body: El domingo hay derbi de filiales y el Real Madrid C quiere vestir sus mejores galas para la exigente visita al Atlético C. Y en este plan de ir con todo al Cerro entra Fran Santamaría. El nuevo 'Joselu' de La Fábrica se ha incorporado a los entrenamientos del segundo filial blanco y todo apunta a que será la gran novedad en la convocatoria para el derbi del domingo. Un perfil de '9' que recuerda mucho al exmadridista Joselu, comparación que se disparó tras su gol al Wanderers en la Intercontinental, donde la propia jugada y el hecho de que acababa de salir del banquillo, recordó a la mítica noche de Joselu ante el Bayern en las semifinales de Champions. El técnico, Marc Carrasco, se apunta al 'efecto Fran', que se ha convertido en la gran sensación en el comienzo de temporada en La Fábrica madridista. Cinco goles en cinco partidos es su tarjeta de presentación. El sorprendente '9', llegado esta temporada del Castellón para incorporarse a la plantilla del Juvenil A (18 años), ha tirado la puerta abajo en menos de un mes de competición oficial. Firmó un doblete en su primer partido, marcó en el segundo, volvió a ver puerta en el tercero (en la Youth League ante el Inter) y revolucionó la Intercontinental marcando el 2-1 al minuto de entrar y provocando un penalti. El pasado miércoles ante el Getafe fue el primer partido en el que se quedó sin marcar. En total, cinco goles en cinco partido para el joven delantero. Ahora le llega la recompensa con el que será su primer ascenso en La Fábrica. Fran Santamaría hizo parte de la pretemporada con el Madrid C, pero la del domingo puede será su primera convocatoria oficial con el segundo filial. El Madrid ha aprovechado que el Juvenil A no juega este fin de semana y la ausencia de Yeremaiah (con la selección sub 18) para promocionar al '9' titularísimo de Álvaro López, que está en un momento de forma impresionante. Una racha de cara a gol que necesita el Madrid C, que ha firmado dos empates sin goles en sus dos primeros partidos. Incluso, no se descarta que inicie el derbi de titular.

articles.title: Timeline: Man City’s Premier League financial charges to reported verdict
articles.summary: City reportedly found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges that were first brought in February 2023.
articles.body:
After years of investigations and hearings, Manchester City have been found guilty of almost all of the 115 alleged breaches of the Premier League’s financial fair play rules, according to reports on Friday.

Below is a timeline of Manchester City’s Premier League financial rules case – from the ‌charges brought in February 2023 to the reported verdict on Friday.

The Premier League refers City to an independent ⁠commission over more than 100 alleged breaches of financial rules.

City were alleged to have committed multiple financial breaches such as failing to provide accurate financial information, Financial Fair Play breaches, failure to cooperate with investigations, breaching profitability and sustainability regulations and failure to report contracts.

City manager Pep Guardiola says the club have already been “condemned” after being charged by the Premier League.

“It’s the same as what happened after UEFA [charges] , these ⁠are just charges. With UEFA, the club proved it was completely innocent. We are lucky we live in a marvellous country where everyone is innocent until proven guilty,” Guardiola said.

In fact, while CAS found that some alleged breaches of overstating sponsorship revenue were not established, other allegations were “time-barred” because they fell outside the five-year statutory limit for prosecution.

CAS also ruled that City showed a “blatant disregard” and “severe” failure to cooperate with UEFA’s investigators.

Guardiola says he would like the financial charges against the club to be dealt with “as soon as possible” after City secured a fifth league title in six seasons under the Spaniard.

“Let’s go. Don’t wait two years. Why don’t we do it quicker? In 24 hours, sit down ⁠with lawyers present. Let’s have it as soon as possible for the benefit of everyone,” he said.

City Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said the club were frustrated by the situation, saying it detracted from the achievements of the team after they achieved a treble.

“I hope people focus and judge them [the players] for their football, what they’re achieving on the pitch and what they’re achieving in every competition they’re in,” he said.

City say they earned revenues of 712.8 million pounds ($876.17m) to June 2023 – an increase of 99.8m (16.3 percent) over the previous season, along with a record net profit of 80.4 million pounds ($106.5m).

Premier League CEO Richard Masters tells the Culture, Media and Sport (CMS) Committee of the UK Parliament that a hearing date has been set for City’s financial rule breach charges.

“There is a date set for that proceeding. Unfortunately, I can’t tell you when that is but it is progressing,” Masters said.

Hearing into City’s alleged violations of the Premier League’s financial regulations begins. Held by an independent commission comprised of three ⁠judges, it is estimated to last 10 weeks.

In a separate independent hearing, both City and the Premier League claimed victory after an ⁠arbitration panel ruled on sponsorship deals, known as Associated Party Transactions (APT), that the club was blocked from completing.

Hearing into City’s alleged violations concludes, with a decision expected in early 2025.

Guardiola said he expected a verdict “in one month”, days after City had spent about 190 million pounds ($251.6m) on new players in the January transfer window.

In advance of the 2025-26 season, Masters says they have no influence over the decision and cannot speculate on the timing of the case.

“Legal processes rarely take less time than anticipated. We have to be patient,” he told Sky ‌Sports.

Guardiola announces he will leave City at the end of the 2025-26 season, bringing to a close a decade in charge that delivered one of the most successful eras in English football.

City appoint former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca as manager from the 2026-27 season, tasking the Italian with building on the success achieved under Guardiola.

Masters acknowledged growing frustration over the delay in a verdict on the alleged charges against City, saying ‌the ‌process had taken longer than expected.

City were found guilty of all but one of the 115 alleged breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, The Athletic and The Times reported on Friday.

The club are expected to appeal, the reports added.

The Premier League declined to comment. “It’s a confidential process, we’re not commenting at all,” a spokesperson said.

City did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment, but told the BBC that the inquiry into allegations “remains ongoing”.

articles.title: A la Rojita se le congela el billete al Europeo
articles.standfirst: La sub 21 tropieza ante Finlandia (2-1) en Tampere y aplaza a la siguiente jornada su clasificación al campeonato que se celebrará el próximo verano
articles.summary: La sub 21 tropieza ante Finlandia (2-1) en Tampere y aplaza a la siguiente jornada su clasificación al campeonato que se celebrará el próximo verano
articles.body: España se quedó sin embarcar en el primer vuelo hacia el Europeo. Se heló en el frío de Tampere y encajó su primera derrota en esta fase de clasificación, la primera también de la 'era Gordo' al frente del equipo. Finlandia, que ya había sacado de quicio a la Rojita en la ida hasta obligarla a remontar, llegó a la cita con la corona del grupo A entre ceja y ceja, dispuesta a arrebatársela a una España que, por su parte, solo pensaba en los tres puntos que le habrían dado el billete. No los logró, y sin embargo no hay motivo para el drama. Finlandia, ahora segunda, se queda a dos puntos, y restan dos compromisos asequibles —San Marino a domicilio y Rumanía en Ibiza— para certificar el pase al Europeo. Que sirva, eso sí, como toque de atención. La Rojita volvió al ruedo tras un paréntesis interminable, el parón más largo y espinoso de cuantos ha tenido que administrar David Gordo. El seleccionador apostó por un once reconocible, con Iker Bravo y Fer López alternándose entre la mediapunta y el costado diestro, y con una de las tres caras nuevas de la convocatoria sobre el césped: Xavi Espart. Y quiso el azar que fuera precisamente por esa banda derecha, un territorio que el catalán no pisa desde la pasada campaña —en el Europeo actuó por dentro y en el Barça lo hace de lateral zurdo—, por donde Finlandia asestó el primer golpe. Moller se coló por ese flanco, escurridizo ante un Espart poco contundente, y la puso atrás para Ruoppi, que definió con la derecha sin que Salvi alcanzara a tapar. Con el susto todavía alojado en el cuerpo, España desenvainó sus armas. El meta finés Jantunen tuvo que emplearse a fondo para salvar a los suyos en un remate de cabeza de Jon Martín, y en el rechace lo intentó Chema Andrés, que también se estrelló contra el guardameta. Fue la ocasión más clara de los de Gordo en la primera parte. España pretendió, poco a poco, sacudirse el dominio finés y adueñarse del cuero, un empeño que no dio los frutos esperados. Es más, volvió a asomarse al precipicio cuando Ruoppi, de nuevo él, armó un disparo que Salvi tapó a bocajarro, providencial, para evitar un correctivo mayor antes de un descanso en el que Chema y Espart, con amarilla ambos, fueron los primeros sustituidos en favor de Mendoza y Ángel Ortiz. Esa fue, a la postre, la perdición de España, que perdió fuelle en el mediocampo y no acertó a generar de la medular hacia arriba. Lo intentó por los exteriores, y de ahí nació un cabezazo de Gonzalo que se perdió lejos de la escuadra de Jantunen, pero poco más dio de sí el repertorio. El jarro de agua fría definitivo cayó en el minuto 66. Gálvez vio el hueco para que Kangasniemi se colase para colgarla al segundo palo desde la izquierda, y allí aguardaba un Álex Valle que no despejó con la contundencia debida y un Ylitolva que empujó a placer el 2-0. Gordo buscó la reacción con los revulsivos Jan Virgili y Pablo García, siempre capaces de revolucionar al equipo desde las bandas, y con Espí, para sumar otra referencia en el área a poco más de un cuarto de hora del final. Fue precisamente el exbético y ahora racinguista quien probó a Jantunen con una falta de media distancia. Pero Finlandia, lejos de encogerse, se fue replegando con la renta de dos goles y echó mano de la malicia para descoser el juego, con esas 'faltitas' de manual que nublaron a la Rojita en su empeño por recortar distancias. No se frustraron los de Gordo, que siguieron percutiendo por fuera y añadieron otra cabeza al área para sumar peligro. Schade has been tracked by several big Premier League clubs for some time, with Chelsea and Tottenham among his admirers, but Arsenal and Liverpool are thought to have been the keenest as the summer transfer window drew to a close.

The Germany international has entered the final two years of his current Brentford deal - signed when he joined from SC Freiburg for £20m in June 2023 - and the west London club are keen to give him improved terms.

articles.title: Former England Striker Andy Carroll Reveals He Was Sexually Assaulted by a Man in 2021
articles.summary: LONDON (AP) — Former Liverpool, Newcastle and England striker Andy Carroll has revealed in his autobiography that he was sexually assaulted by a man in 2021 and still struggles to deal with the ordeal.
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — Former Liverpool, Newcastle and England striker Andy Carroll has revealed in his autobiography that he was sexually assaulted by a man in 2021 and still struggles to deal with the ordeal.

Carroll's autobiography, called 'Owning It', was published on Thursday and in it the 37-year-old Englishman details the attack at his home in Newcastle, which led to the perpetrator reportedly being jailed for three years.

"Something happened to me a few years ago that was so traumatic I only decided to include it in this book at the very last minute," he wrote in the book, extracts of which have been published in the British press.

Report: Manchester City GUILTY on 114 Charges

"I was sexually assaulted, there I said it. Scary to even think about and only a few people knew about it before now."

Carroll was also tormented by the prospect of talking about what happened before finally deciding to include it in the book, after speaking at length with his girlfriend.

"Me and Lou spent a lot of time discussing whether to mention it in this book or not," he said. "Scary to talk about but it's made (me) the person I am today as much as any of the good stuff. And if me talking about it helps just one person then good, it will have been worth it."

The mental anguish continued long after the attack, which happened after a friend of his former partner came to his home to watch a boxing match and was set to stay overnight.

Carroll details how he threw the man — who he said was a "celebrity mate" — out of the house and then "smacked him unconscious" when he tried to come back in. He then called the police.

"What happened to me affected every facet of my life. I'd think about it every day, making it difficult to focus on anything else, including football," he said. "The trauma of what happened to me hasn't gone away."

Carroll cost Liverpool 35 million pounds ($46 million) when he joined from Newcastle in January 2011. Back then, he was the Premier League's most expensive British transfer signing.

He also played for West Ham in the Premier League, and scored twice for England, including one goal at the European Championship in 2012.

At the end of his professional career, Carroll played briefly in France with Amiens and Bordeaux before joining non-league Dagenham and Redbridge in England, scoring six goals last season.

articles.title: Un Kvaratskhelia total para reclamar el Balón de Oro
articles.standfirst: El georgiano completó la temporada 2025-26 con 19 goles y 10 asistencias, pero su impacto fue mucho más allá: desequilibrio, creación, trabajo defensivo, cinco títulos y el reconocimiento como mejor jugador de la Champions League
articles.summary: El georgiano completó la temporada 2025-26 con 19 goles y 10 asistencias, pero su impacto fue mucho más allá: desequilibrio, creación, trabajo defensivo, cinco títulos y el reconocimiento como mejor jugador de la Champions League
articles.body: La carrera por el Balón de Oro 2026 entra en su recta decisiva con Khvicha Kvaratskhelia entre los 30 nominados. En su segunda temporada en el Paris SaintGermain, el georgiano construyó una candidatura que va mucho más allá de sus 29 contribuciones de gol Estas cifras representan únicamente la parte más visible de su influencia. Su temporada destacó especialmente por todo el trabajo que precede al gol: eliminar rivales, hacer progresar al equipo, generar situaciones de remate, disputar duelos y contribuir defensivamente. En Ligue 1 completó 2,79 regates por cada 90 minutos, con un 59% de efectividad, y produjo 2,06 pases clave por 90 minutos. Esa capacidad para generar peligro se mantuvo en el máximo escenario europeo. En Champions League realizó 50 disparos, el tercer registro más alto de toda la competición 2025/26. Además, completó 30 regates, reflejo de una producción ofensiva que no dependió exclusivamente de la finalización. La dimensión de su temporada también aparece en su trabajo defensivo, un aspecto especialmente significativo tratándose de un futbolista de ataque. En Ligue 1, Kvaratskhelia ganó 103 duelos terrestres, una media de 6,25 por cada 90 minutos, y añadió 24 entradas y 10 intercepciones. Ese compromiso defensivo se trasladó también a Europa, donde registró otras 17 entradas en Champions League. Son cifras que permiten ampliar la lectura de su rendimiento: Kvaratskhelia no solo intervino cuando el PSG tuvo la posesión. Disputó, presionó, interceptó y participó activamente en el trabajo defensivo y la recuperación, combinándolo con un elevado volumen de acciones ofensivas. El reglamento del Balón de Oro establece tres criterios de elección y los ordena expresamente por importancia: primero, las actuaciones individuales y el carácter decisivo e impresionante; segundo, el rendimiento colectivo y los títulos conseguidos; y tercero, la clase y el fair play. La temporada de Kvaratskhelia ofrece argumentos para ser analizada desde esas tres dimensiones. En el rendimiento individual, su producción no se limita a los 19 goles y 10 asistencias. A ellos suma desequilibrio en el uno contra uno, generación de ocasiones, progresión con balón y trabajo defensivo. En Champions, terminó además con 10 goles y 6 asistencias, participando directamente en 16 goles, y estableció una secuencia inédita al convertirse en el primer jugador en marcar o asistir en siete partidos consecutivos de una misma fase eliminatoria de la competición. Su actuación recibió además el reconocimiento de la propia UEFA, cuyo Grupo de Observadores Técnicos lo eligió Jugador de la Temporada de la Champions League 2025/26. En el segundo criterio, rendimiento colectivo y palmarés, Kvaratskhelia formó parte de un Paris Saint-Germain que conquistó cinco títulos durante el periodo evaluado: Champions League, Ligue 1, Supercopa de Europa, Copa Intercontinental de la FIFA y Trophée des Champions. Y el tercer criterio, clase y fair play, completa una valoración que no se limita a estadísticas o trofeos, sino que contempla también el comportamiento deportivo del futbolista. La combinación de los tres criterios permite analizar la temporada de Kvaratskhelia en toda su amplitud: rendimiento individual, influencia en diferentes fases del juego, éxito colectivo y comportamiento deportivo. La ausencia de Georgia en el Mundial de 2026 introduce una circunstancia particular en la candidatura de Kvaratskhelia, pero existe un precedente histórico. Kevin Keegan es el único futbolista que ha ganado el Balón de Oro en un año de Mundial sin que su selección disputase el torneo. Ocurrió en 1978. Inglaterra no consiguió clasificarse para el Mundial de Argentina, pero el rendimiento de Keegan con el Hamburgo terminó imponiéndose en la valoración de los votantes de France Football. Casi medio siglo después, Kvaratskhelia afronta una circunstancia similar. Georgia no participa en el Mundial de 2026, por lo que el peso de su candidatura recae fundamentalmente en una temporada de clubes en la que combinó producción ofensiva, creación, desequilibrio, trabajo defensivo, títulos y rendimiento en los grandes partidos. El contexto y el sistema de elección de 1978 eran diferentes a los actuales, pero el precedente de Keegan demuestra que la ausencia del Mundial no ha supuesto históricamente un impedimento absoluto para conquistar el Balón de Oro. Una temporada completa en la que Kvaratskhelia se postula como uno de los candidatos principales para alzarse con tan prestigioso trofeo como el Balón de Oro.

articles.title: A la espera de la condena del siglo: de multa a la expulsión de la Premier
articles.standfirst: El Manchester City espera la decisión del tribunal tras ser considerado culpable
articles.summary: El Manchester City espera la decisión del tribunal tras ser considerado culpable
articles.body: El fútbol inglés contiene la respiración ante la que se espera que sea la condena del siglo en el deporte británico. Aunque el veredicto del juicio contra el Manchester City aún no es público, el bombazo de The Athletic a media tarde del viernes hizo saltar los cimientos de la Premier League: "El Manchester City ha sido declarado culpable en prácticamente todas las acusaciones relacionadas con infracciones de las regulaciones financieras de la Premier League". Inmediatamente, la mente de los aficionados al fútbol (sobre todo los del Manchester City) se va hacia la condena. ¿Qué va a pasar con el Manchester City ahora? Esa es la gran duda, la gran pregunta que la Comisión Independiente que estudia el caso debe resolver en los próximos días y que cambiará (o no) el panorama del fútbol inglés. Al tratarse de un caso tan masivo (se dice que el City será declarado culpable de 114 de los 115 cargos de los que estaba acusado), no hay precedentes ni muchas pistas de lo que el tribunal puede dictaminar, aunque los medios ingleses han dado durante estos años de proceso varias opciones sobre lo que puede pasar a continuación. Dejando claro que es un terreno especulativo, las posibles sanciones se mueven en tres grandes pilares: deducción de puntos, sanciones económicas o, la más dura de todas, la expulsión de la Premier League o del sistema del fútbol inglés. Una sanción económica sería el castigo más leve, aunque la cuantía de la misma pueda ser igualmente severa. Según TeamTalk, citando una fuente interna de un club de la Premier, esta sería la condena que el resto de clubes creen que será la definitiva. "Los aficionados de todo el mundo estarán clamando y quizás esperando el descenso y grandes deducciones de puntos, pero por lo que estamos escuchando como club, en este momento esperamos una multa", cuenta esa fuente. Kieran Maguire, experto en el mundo de las finanzas del fútbol, ha explicado en BBC que sería la sanción 'ideal' para el conjunto del Etihad: "Si el Manchester City ha sido declarado culpable, estarían encantados si solo se les impusiera una multa. Pero espero que otros clubes y la mayoría de los comentaristas anticipen algún tipo de deducción de puntos, si no algo peor. Podría haber una larga serie de litigios por parte de clubes que consideren que se han visto perjudicados durante el periodo en el que el Manchester City infringió las normas". En el único caso que se puede antojar similar, el Chelsea fue sancionado este verano con diez millones de libras y sin poder fichar durante dos ventanas de traspasos (aunque este castigo quedó en suspenso) por unas infracciones derivadas de la época de Roman Abramovich. Sin embargo, el caso no es comparable puesto que fue la nueva propiedad del club blue la que se autoinculpó y colaboró con la Premier en la investigación. El City siempre ha negado los cargos. En cuanto a la deducción de puntos, hay dos vertientes: una sanción lo suficientemente importante como para provocar el descenso directo del club o diferir esa sanción en varias temporadas, lo que complicaría su participación en la Champions League durante algunos años. Otros clubes como el Everton o el Nottingham Forest han sufrido la deducción de puntos por problemas relacionados con el fair-play financiero de la Premier, pero la magnitud del caso del City invita a pensar en una cantidad de puntos inusual y que pueda, efectivamente, llevar al descenso inmediato al club. Un caso más extremo, aunque posible, es el de la expulsión directa de la Premier League del club de Mánchester. La Comisión Independiente podría dictaminar que la gravedad de los cargos y su número son merecedores de una sanción ejemplar y la expulsión del City es un escenario que no se descarta pese a las implicaciones que tendría en patrocinios, contratos de televisión de la Premier y demás partidas económicas para los clubes ingleses. Hay quienes, incluso, piden que esa expulsión no se limite a la Premier y se excluya al Manchester City del sistema de la EFL (English Football League), es decir, descender al club por debajo de la League Two, que es el cuarto escalafón del fútbol inglés, y obligar al City a reiniciar su historia en la National League. Es de esperar que la condena no llegue a esos niveles, pero hasta que el veredicto no sea oficial y se conozca el castigo, la especulación seguirá abierta. Y luego está la posible retirada de los títulos ganados en esa etapa (2009-2018), las denuncias de los clubes que se sientan perjudicados... El caso está cerca de definirse, pero lejos de cerrarse.

articles.title: USMNT teen Cavan Sullivan could make his senior debut as Mauricio Pochettino gives young players a look against Peru
articles.summary: Sullivan, 16, would be the youngest player to debut for the U.S. since Freddy Adu in 2006 if he appears against Peru on Saturday.
articles.body:
ORLANDO — After spending the week with a new wave of U.S. soccer prospects, after the morning workouts, personal meetings and bonding exercises highlighted by singing performances some much better than others — coach Mauricio Pochettino has gained a better understanding of his youthful roster.

It's to the point where he seems confident enough to throw many of them into the first U.S. match since the World Cup, a friendly against Peru on Saturday afternoon.

Given the short amount of time leading to the first of four tests over 11 days, many veterans are better positioned to start. But with 11 subs permitted and Pochettino's desire to integrate players at the start of the cycle leading to the 2030 World Cup, the U.S. is sure to have a young look for much of the match.

Specifically, the fan base is eager to see 16-year-old forward Cavan Sullivan , who, if he gets onto the field, would become the youngest to make his USMNT debut since Freddy Adu , also 16, in 2006.

Based on Sullivan's breakout season with the Philadelphia Union , "he's ready, but the rest of the players too are ready," Pochettino said Friday. "Of course, we are going to mix a little bit with some new players — or young players — with senior players. That's important, that mix [and] hope that that works. In the rest of the game too; that is our idea."

Speaking on the group at large, Pochettino added, "We are in a very good place. Talking about Cavan, he's doing really well in Philadelphia, and that's why he's here. He's mature enough on the field to be there and to compete."

Sullivan — a youth international more than two years into his pro career that will take him to Manchester City when he turns 18 — was among a dozen players invited to their first senior camp.

Sullivan seems to fit in well with the established players.

"He's very quiet. I think he's probably a little nervous," said World Cup defender Alex Freeman , who, at 22, is older than 12 of his 27 teammates. "He's very driven. He wants to be able to get better. … His ceiling is going to be [over] the roof, knowing he's already succeeded in MLS. Now, what can you do with the national team? How can you come in and make an impact?"

Sullivan has not been made available for interviews during camp but is expected to talk about his experiences once he has debuted.

The Americans will also play Chile on Tuesday in St. Louis , Mexico on Oct. 3 in greater Phoenix and Canada on Oct. 6 in St. Paul, Minn.

Sullivan and the other young players are vying to not only earn callbacks for the full senior camps in November and March, but continue making their mark ahead of the 2028 Olympics, which is largely limited to players 23 and under. Olympic coach Steve Cherundolo, who has attended this senior gathering, is expected to conduct a U-23 camp later this year.

"They are showing their real talent because they have an amazing capacity and quality," Pochettino said. "The energy was amazing. It was really contagious. … After talking to them, you feel younger. It's true, it's true! … It's very nice to feel that. It's [been] a long time since I felt this way working with a group of players. That is amazing for us, for the present and the future."

Pochettino's first aim was getting to know the new players; he had never met some.

"What they like, what they don't like, how they are, how they live, how the families are," he said.

Then he learned more about their approach to the game and where they fit into the team.

"It's so important too that they need to know what we expect from them," Pochettino said.

Pochettino also monitored body language.

He said he asks players, "You are ready?"

A player might vocalize affirmatively but subtly shake his head side to side as well, Pochettino demonstrated in his news conference at Inter&Co Stadium.

He called the mix of young and older players "very organic and natural now after a few days."

He added, "It's a group of players you don't feel that someone is [here] for the first time or someone who has 100 caps. That is an important thing. Of course, the younger [players] show tremendous respect to the senior players. They are humble enough to listen, but also the senior players are so good in the way they treat the young kids and because they also show respect to them. When the respect is reciprocal, that is the best way to build an excellent relationship."

Justin Ellis , a 19-year-old forward for Orlando City in his first camp, said last week that Gio Reyna , who is just 23, was his favorite player growing up.

"It does make you feel a little bit old," Reyna said this week.

After being reminded of his own comment Friday, Ellis was a little embarrassed. But then he said, Reyna has been "so good to me. … We see the game in a similar way. We both love playing with the ball. I think we can connect really well when we're on the field. He's really taking me under his wing."

Use our code STS10 to get 10% off your first order and find your new favorite Clemson gear today!

Shakin' the Southland:We're in year 3 of the Cal Golden Bears playing in the ACC. How are fans enjoying it? Have the fans learned to embrace the new rivalries or is there a desire to find a way to go back to playing other West Coast schools?

Writing for California I think fans are glad to be somewhere and on the upswing. Things were looking pretty dire around the dissolving of the Pac 12. I think more regional play would be great but there's some hard feelings about being bailed on. I think it's been interesting to watch Stanford and Cal become more intertwined on a destiny level.

STS: Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele is the guy everyone is talking about in regards to Cal. Who else on this Bears team should Clemson fans be aware of going into Friday night?

WFC: Safety room is stacked, it's not just Lopa. The DB play hasn't fallen off since Wilcox's exit which is great to see. Nate Burrell has been making some plays. I like Cooper Perry as a receiver, he's going to get more work as things progress I think.

STS: How did fans react to the hire of Tosh Lupoi? Are fans pretty confident in him despite this being his first head coaching job?

WFC: He was the chosen son and the unifying name for a couple years before he was even hired. There's definitely lore about how he left that was brought up before the possibility was real, but once things got real thats who everyone wanted and thats who they got. In an insane turnover year where a lot of blue blood types were poaching I was more interested in finding a passionate coordinator who isn't confused by how to be successful here. I think this is a region where knowing it has and can work here is important and some coaches have never been able to picture what this place can be. I graduated from Berkeley High in 05 and this place was full and the team was good, it's all there for the taking.

STS: An under-discussed side of the Luke Ferrelli saga is him leaving Cal. How does Cal go about keeping their star players from hitting the portal, particularly with a guy like JKS? Has the portal era generally been good or bad for Cal?

WFC: This is where it's nice to have Tosh. Everyone's heard the story of him flying straight from his intro presser and going to JKS's parents living room. He really was wearing the exact same outfit. Knowing there's a maniac who thinks about it more than I do is cool. You don't worry about him "getting" the new era. He's built for this era I think. This portal cycle felt rich and cool but I think they're going to try to recruit and retain more in the future.

STSL For Tiger fans making the trip this week, what do you recommend they do in the Berkeley area? Any pregame spots that are a must?

WFC: Campus bars you've got Raleighs for adults and Kips or Henrys for the kids. If you're in town on Saturday and wanna watch games Kingfish on the Oakland stretch for Telegraph is the (blue and) gold standard. If you're just by the game and don't wanna think too hard, get Mexican food at Tacos Sinaloa, maybe grab a Sonoran dog from a vendor as you leave the game, they're bomb. If you wanna get fancier check out the "gourmet ghetto" in North Berkeley, stuff like Chez Panisse. The classic burger spot in Berkeley is Smokehouse but The Station is right in the shadow of the Claremont and while bougie is a nice neighborhood Cal spot. Pizza check out Rose or Pizza De Laura around Shattuck.

STS: A lot of people want to talk about this being a "culture clash" of two different fan bases. What are some misconceptions about Cal fans and what do you wish more people knew about the Cal football culture?

WFC: We're pretty fun, man. The faithful party more than you'd expect. We can take a joke, just be cool

WFC: Run the ball successfully, the line needs to give Mohammed a little more space so we can get more explosives, he's really talented. Obviously we'd love to see JKS get another second or two in the pocket and for the catching issues to resolve themselves. Curious if we'll see more Dorian Thomas looks.

STS: Where can the folks find your work?

WriteforCalifornia.com ! Also shout out to "Tell the Whole Damn World" pod, who have me on most Wednesdays this fall

Shout out to Jesse for taking his time to talk with us. For any Tigers fans in Berkley for the game, I'm sure his recommendations will come in handy!

articles.summary: Todos los detalles de lo ocurrido en el conjunto 'cityzen' entre el 2009 y el 2018
articles.body: Saltó la bomba en el Manchester City.
